summary: The agent passed all eight criteria. It loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, read NOTES.md and the UI guidelines, and kept going after an auto-compaction mid-session. It called the task scoped and said it would keep the design in chat. It asked its non-visual questions as terminal options. When the question of where the filters go came up, it started the visual companion on its own and wrote placement.html showing three layouts (A: filter bar above the table, B: popover, C: side panel). It gave me a localhost URL and asked me to reply in the terminal. After I picked A, it showed the full design in chat, asked for approval, and began implementing once I said yes. No spec or plan document was written.
reasoning: The log and the disk state back up every criterion. Without being asked, the agent decided the layout question needed to be shown and opened the companion at that point. It kept the task bounded with no spec or plan, got my pick and then approval in the terminal, and started implementing.

observations.description: On first launch Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available — Currently pinned: Opus 5, Latest: Opus 5.5' prompt even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No. The header then showed 'Opus 5.5', so the prompt looks misleading or redundant.

Auto-compaction ran twice: once while it was reading guidelines before the first question, and again right after I approved the design. The status line showed '0% until auto-compact' early on. After each compaction the skill was restored ('Skills restored (hyperpowers:brainstorming)').

The agent noticed that .hyperpowers/ isn't in .gitignore and that the mockups land in the repo root, so they could get committed by accident. It flagged this to the user without editing the file, which is good. The companion could default to a gitignored or temp location.

The agent asked four rounds of terminal questions before the visual one, including two scope-creep choices (fixing the existing no-JS problem, converting old CSS to tokens). That's reasonable under CLAUDE.md, but it adds turns to a bounded task. It also chose to bundle an unrelated 'fix:' commit for the CSS tokens.
Its message said 'The companion is token-intensive. Say so if you'd rather stay in the terminal.' That's a useful opt-out, though it's somewhat odd wording to show a user.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" right after the prompt. The session log's only Skill tool_use is {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}.

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened: start-server.sh run, localhost URL given, HTML screen of candidate layouts written
criteria.evidence:
Log Bash: ".../skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir "$PWD" --open". It wrote .hyperpowers/brainstorm/81917-1793827643/content/placement.html (91 lines, starting "

Where should the filters go on the Account activity page?

", options A/B/C with mockups). Screen: "I've opened the placement question in a browser tab: http://localhost:61875/?key=490a73d4...".

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time; non-visual questions not routed through the browser
criteria.evidence: The log order is: 4 AskUserQuestion calls in the terminal (which filters, what counts as Security changes, no-JS scope, old CSS cleanup), then start-server.sh, then the Write of placement.html. No companion was mentioned or started before the placement question, and the only content screens are waiting.html and placement.html.

Screen: "Since this is a scoped change to an existing page, I'll outline the filter options here rather than write a full spec." The final design summary (files touched, commits, testing) stayed in chat.
`find coding-agent-workdir/docs -path '*specs*' -o -path '*plans*'` returned nothing. `ls docs` shows only ui-guidelines. `git status --short` shows only `?? .hyperpowers/`.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The only Skill tool_use in the log is hyperpowers:brainstorming. No plans dir or plan file exists on disk (same find as above). The 11 'writing-plans' string hits in the log come from the loaded skill text, not from any invocation.

criteria.criterion: Approval of the layout asked before implementation code
criteria.evidence: It said "I recommend A. Take a look, click one if you like, and reply here." and then, after my pick, asked "Shall I go ahead with this design?". `git status` showed no edits to public/ before my approval.

After "Yes, go ahead." the screen showed "Showing current page files and stylesheet links" and the log showed it reading the guidelines and public/activity.css/html for the build. It had earlier laid out commits: fix: tokens, feat: filters, docs: NOTES.
